findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no measurable concentration in sanitizer bucket. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) remade sanitizer bucket to a concentration of 100 ppm Chlorine bleach. Ensure sanitizer buckets are made at a frequency to sustain the concentration as reccomended by the manufacturer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Two open gallons of 1% milk observed in the 2 door cooler past their expiration dates of 10/24/2023, and without any written open dates. CORRECTED- These were from several days when milk cartons were unavailable. Gallons of milk were voluntarily discarded. 
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date. (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food. (D) Approved date marking systems. (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container. [Pf]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment: Evidence of rodent activity was observed in the dry storage room. Droppings were observed on the floor along walls and in corners. Clean up droppings and coordinate efforts with the pest control provider to keep rodents out of the kitchen and dry storage areas.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions. [Pf]

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed for handwashing, food service based on risk classification, and lack of adherence to the established time control policy. Evidence of rodent activity was also observed in the dry storage room. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at the follow-up inspection at the end of the month.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 Signed reporting agreements were not available for employees that work lunch service. Employee health policy was discussed, and reporting agreements were signed by staff. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring and sign reporting agreements prior to beginning their first shift. Maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for staff that work in the kitchen.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 PIC did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to handle portioned foods for lunches. Just prior to putting on gloves a bleach solution was prepared. Handwashing was discussed, and employee was observed washing hands between tasks as needed for the remainder of the inspection. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Also, hands must be washed after engaging in any activities that contaminate the hands and prior to putting on gloves to handle food.

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.citation_text:
3-201.11 School is Class II medium risk and has been operating as a Class I high risk. Leftover hot foods received for hot lunch service have been cooled and kept for additional service. Foods observed in the cooler today included portions of chicken and rice and steamed broccoli. All foods were discarded during inspection. Ensure hot TCS foods are served or discarded by the end of lunch service. **See HACCP section for additional information**
Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with the law.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 General surfaces and stored equipment, which includes trays and tubs in the dry storage room, need to be cleaned and sanitized due to the observation of rodent activity. Clean and sanitize the dry storage room before the follow-up inspection.
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.citation_text:
3-501.19 PIC has been keeping leftover cold and hot TCS foods at the conclusion of lunch service. The school has a posted time control policy stating foods are picked up for service at 10:30am and are to be discarded by no later than 2:30pm. Lunch service is done daily by 12:30pm. All hot and cold TCS foods must be served or discarded by the end of lunch service based on this policy and lack of temperature control for foods during lunch service. Leftover TCS foods observed in the cooler included a deli meat and cheese sandwich, meatless chili portions, steamed broccoli portion, and chicken and rice portions. All foods were discarded during inspection. **See HACCP section for additional information** 
If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours the food shall be cooked and served, served at any temperature if ready-to-eat, or discarded, within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 Evidence of rodent activity was observed in the dry storage room. Droppings were observed on the floor along walls and in corners. Droppings were also observed on a tray and in a bus tub on a cart. What appeared to possibly be urine was also observed along one of the walls. Maintenance was made aware of the issue. Pest control operator will be contacted for service.
The premises shall be maintained free of pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence by routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies; routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests; using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13; and eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Pre-dampened wiping cloths used to wipe down lunch tables by students between lunch shifts were observed sitting on trays. A couple of the wiping cloths dried out to the point they didn’t register a concentration for the presence of bleach solution. Wiping cloths were placed in bleach solution again to re-wet prior to use. Storage of wiping cloths in bleach solution between uses was discussed. Ensure wiping cloths are left in bleach solution until just prior to when children will need them to wipe down tables. Provide wet wiping cloths as needed, and store in bleach solution between uses. 
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Bleach solution for wiping down surfaces in the kitchen was not available. Bleach solution at 200ppm was provided. Ensure a bleach solution is available and ready to use prior to beginning lunch service. 
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Floor in the dry storage room was soiled with rodent droppings and other general buildup of dust and debris. Clean the floor prior to the follow-up inspection.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Current person overseeing food service has a food handler certification. The need for a certified food manager on-site during lunch service was discussed. The food service position is currently vacant but will be filled for the next school year. Staff were encouraged to have another person in addition to the new cook obtain a food manager certification to ensure a CFM is present during hours of operation for lunch.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 Cook has a food handler certification. Cook and principal were advised that a manager certification is now required for the person in charge of food service per the FDA Food Code. Cook and any other staff that cover the lunch service when cook is absent need to be certified food managers. 

Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Cook was observed preparing to put on gloves to handle food without first washing hands. Multiple surfaces were touched after removing the pair of gloves he was wearing previously. Proper hand washing between tasks and prior to putting on gloves were discussed.  

Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Also, hands must be washed after engaging in any activities that contaminate the hands and prior to putting on gloves to handle food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11(C) Can opener had black gooey buildup along the top edge of the blade. Cook used the can opener prior to inspector's arrival to open fruit cocktail. Proper cleaning and sanitizing was discussed. The blade was wiped down and sanitized during the inspection. Cook was advised to clean and sanitize the can opener with all other utensils and equipment at the conclusion of lunch service. 

Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned and sanitized between uses and up to every 4hrs after continuous use.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-202.12 Spray bottle of bleach solution was observed at a concentration so strong that it bleached out the test strip and began to turn it white. Cook was advised on proper use of the two bleach products available. Solution was diluted to be at 200ppm chlorine. Follow label directions and use test strips to verify proper sanitizing concentration (150-200ppm). 

Poisonous or toxic materials shall be used according to manufacturer's use directions included in labeling and in a manner that does not pose a hazard to people or risk of contamination of food, single service articles, and clean equipment.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Plastic container used for storing knives in the dry storage room was observed to be soiled with general debris and dead insects in the bottom. Container and knives were removed to be cleaned and sanitized. Cleaning of the storage container and/or use of a covered container were discussed. 

Clean utensils and equipment shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.
